text:
Priya Rao: Escalating a customer issue — Acme's integration keeps getting disconnected when consuming long SSE responses from our /v1/generate/stream endpoint. They report partial outputs followed by a socket error. Ticket attached: ACME-9876.
Alex Chen: thanks. any logs from the customer or our ingress?
Priya Rao: they sent a client stack trace and our proxy + runtime logs. Client sees repeated "socket hang up" then reconnects and sometimes duplicates the last event. They say it happens when they throttle read speed (they're consuming ~10KB/s).
Alex Chen: that sounds like backpressure / slow consumer. Do we have server-side write errors?
Support Bot: [attached] runtime/error.log excerpt:
```
2026-02-28T14:12:03Z ERROR write EPIPE on connection conn=0x7f9a3c1b
2026-02-28T14:12:03Z WARN client disconnected: reason=read timeout, remote=10.2.1.45
2026-02-28T14:12:03Z INFO aborting stream for req_id=req_4f2f due to socket write failure
```
Luis Gomez: those EPIPEs mean the kernel dropped the connection while we were writing. Usually happens when the client stops reading and the send queue fills. For SSE the server keeps streaming, but if the consumer is slow we must respect backpressure and wait for the socket to drain. Are we forcing writes without checking drain?
Alex Chen: runtime engine is mostly C++ but the HTTP layer is Node-based for our edge service. We flush chunk every token batch (pipelined). I can check if we ignore the writable.write() return value or miss listening for 'drain'.
Priya Rao: customer provided a repro. Steps they used (condensed):
1) curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate/stream -d '{"prompt":"long streaming test","max_tokens":20000}' 
2) pipe through pv to limit read: `pv -L 10k`
3) after ~30s they consistently see partial output (last 2 events) then connection reset, client reconnects and gets duplicate events

Alex Chen: perfect. pv is a great way to simulate slow client. I can repro locally.

EngOncall Bot: note: ALB idle timeout default=60s, NGINX proxy_read_timeout=60s in prod. If streaming goes longer than that with slow reads, upstream may close.
Luis Gomez: good call. But customer says it fails inside 30s, so likely not ALB idle timeout. More likely kernel send buffer + our write pattern. Check for CLOSE_WAIT / backlog in netstat.

Priya Rao: attached their netstat snapshot: many connections in ESTABLISHED, some in CLOSE_WAIT, backlog queue near limit.

Alex Chen: here's what I found reproducing locally: when I throttle consumer to 10KB/s, after ~22s node process emits EPIPE and we call abortStream() which closes the socket. That leads to client reconnect and our server doesn't track last-event-id, so duplicates happen.

Alex Chen: minimal repro command I used:
```
# start a local proxy/edge pointing to our runtime
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -X POST https://local.redwood/v1/generate/stream -d '{"prompt":"stream test","max_tokens":10000}' | pv -L 10k > /dev/null
```

Luis Gomez: root causes to consider:
- We may be writing without honoring backpressure (ignoring write() return and not waiting for 'drain')
- NGINX/ALB timeouts or proxy buffering closing sockets earlier than we expect
- Kernel send buffer exhaustion (tune net.core.wmem_max / tcp_wmem)
- File descriptor limits / too many concurrent slow consumers leading to resource constraints

Priya Rao: customer asks for workarounds ASAP. What quick mitigations can we offer?

Alex Chen: immediate mitigation we can recommend to the customer:
- Use exponential backoff on reconnect and include Last-Event-ID to de-duplicate (SSE provides id field).
- Avoid arbitrarily throttling — increase client read buffer.
- If using ALB/NGINX, set proxy_read_timeout and keepalive to a higher value and disable proxy_buffering for SSE: `proxy_buffering off; proxy_cache off;`

Luis Gomez: on our side short-term fixes:
- Patch Node edge to respect writable.write() return and pause token emission until 'drain' fires. That prevents EPIPE and keeps connection open longer.
- Add rate-limiting per-connection for token emission when client read rate is low (adaptive throttling).
- Add last-event-id support so reconnects don't replay full context.

Alex Chen: I've got a draft fix to check write() return and await drain. I'm testing with the pv throttle now. If it works, we can rollout to canary edge.

Priya Rao: customer-facing note: I drafted a reply with temporary mitigations and asked them to try `curl -N` and increase their client buffer. I asked for tcpdump if problems persist.

Support Bot: customer replied: "We tested with bigger buffer and it improved but still saw occasional resets under heavy load (many parallel streams)."

Luis Gomez: parallel slow consumers is a different failure mode. If too many conns use up file descriptors or queuing, you'll see server aborts. We should instrument per-node open fd count, netstat backlog, and token queue lengths.

Alex Chen: can we do a small canary: apply Node fix + NGINX config change (proxy_buffering off, increase proxy_read_timeout to 300s) on a subset of edge hosts and route Acme traffic there?

EngOncall Bot: approved for canary on hosts edge-canary-1..3. Make sure to set health-check timeouts.

Priya Rao: plan: (1) Alex pushes patch to edge: await drain before more writes (PR #4231), (2) infra updates NGINX for SSE endpoints on canary hosts, (3) monitor metrics: EPIPE count, ESTABLISHED/CLOSE_WAIT ratio, open fd count, and duplicate-events from customer logs.

Alex Chen: status update: local tests with write-await-drain + pv -L 10k show no EPIPE after 2 minutes, tokens slow down but keep flowing. I'll open PR and add tests simulating backpressure.

Luis Gomez: longer-term: consider switching streaming API to use WebSocket or HTTP/2 server push which have more explicit flow-control semantics. Also add backpressure telemetry on the runtime to detect slow consumers and apply adaptive batching.

Priya Rao: customer update sent. They asked for ETA — I'll give tentative 48–72h for canary and monitoring, and escalation to 24h if they say it's production-blocking.

Alex Chen: I'll assign myself PR, tag @Luis for review. Quick notes for the patch:
- don't call `res.end()` on write error; instead mark stream as stalled and try graceful backoff
- ensure we attach `socket.setNoDelay(true)` to reduce Nagle delays (helps small writes)
- add a per-connection `maxBufferedBytes` threshold and stop emitting tokens when above it

Support Bot: created ticket INFRA-1753 for NGINX change, and RUNTIME-2219 for write-drain fix.

Priya Rao: closing loop: customer acknowledged the plan and will test canary traffic next day. I'll keep thread updated. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

Alex Chen: will post PR link when ready.

Luis Gomez: leaving a small checklist for post-mitigation monitoring:
- decrease in EPIPE and socket errors
- lower duplicate-event counts reported by customer
- stable ESTABLISHED -> FIN transitions, fewer CLOSE_WAIT states
- no large spike in memory due to paused per-connection buffers

Priya Rao: noted. tagging this resolved-for-now until canary results.
